premises: Cryo-rolling suppresses recrystallization in the B2 phase while promoting recovery, creating a hierarchical microstructure with fine lamellar and coarse non-lamellar regions.
The semi-coherent phase boundaries in the eutectic HEA are strong enough to accommodate high stress and enable interphase deformation compatibility.
A brief anneal after cryo-rolling can produce partially recovered, softened interlamellar boundaries that reduce dislocation pile-ups.
Refining the lamellar architecture to an ultrafine scale will reduce local stress concentrations and prevent microcracking.
The proposed treatment will simultaneously increase room-temperature tensile ductility and maintain or increase yield strength.
